title: Why do some roads have rumble strips?
sources: Federal Highway Administration Rumble Strip Overview

lines.text: Why do highways have those textured grooves cut into the shoulder that make a loud buzzing vibration?
lines.caps: Why do highway shoulders have *loud | buzzing *grooves?

lines.text: Those grooves are called rumble strips, and they are one of the most effective safety inventions on Earth.
lines.caps: They're called *rumble strips | and they save thousands of *lives!

lines.text: Fatigue and distraction cause thousands of drivers to unintentionally drift off the roadway.
lines.caps: Drowsy drivers often *drift | toward ditches and *guardrails

lines.text: When vehicle tires roll over the milled asphalt grooves, it creates intense tactile vibrations and a loud drone.
lines.caps: Tires hit grooves creating *intense | vibration and *sound

lines.text: This physical jolt instantly shocks drowsy or inattentive drivers awake before they crash into trees.
Federal studies show rumble strips reduce fatal run-off-the-road crashes by over thirty-five percent.
Those humble grooves in the pavement silently save thousands of lives every single year.
lines.caps: Simple grooves keeping *drivers | alive every single *day!
